primary_source.headline: Cabinet approves five Rs 10,021 crore railway multitracking projects across four states
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Wednesday approved five major multitracking projects covering 17 districts in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana at an estimated cost of Rs 10,021 crore.The projects will expand the Indian Railways network by approximately 540 km. They comprise the Whitefield–Bangarapet third and fourth lines (47 km), Arakkonam–Renigunta third and fourth lines (77 km), Hosur–Omalur doubling (147 km), Salem–Karur–Dindigul doubling (159 km), and multitracking of the Secunderabad (Ghatkesar)–Kazipet section (110 km).Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw informed the media that the projects have been planned under the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan. The focus is on enhancing multi-modal connectivity and logistics efficiency through integrated planning and stakeholder consultations. “These projects will provide seamless connectivity for the movement of people, goods and services,” he said.Railways spent 80% of gross budgetary support in first three quarters of current fiscalThe increased line capacity will significantly enhance mobility, improve operational efficiency and ensure greater service reliability. The works are expected to streamline operations and ease congestion on busy routes.They will also strengthen rail connectivity to nearly 2,121 villages with a combined population of about 52 lakh people, he said. In addition, the projects will improve access to several prominent tourist destinations, including Tirupati, Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Tiruttani, Sri Padmavati Ammavaari Temple at Tiruchanur, Kotilingeshwara Devaalaya, Bangaru Tirupati, Kolar Gold Fields and Hogenakkal Falls. These corridors are essential for transporting coal, cement, iron and steel, containers, automobiles, food grains, petroleum products and fertilisers.The capacity augmentation is projected to generate additional freight traffic of 47 million tonnes per annum, supporting industrial growth and economic activity in the region, the Minister said.

primary_source.headline: 'Won't allow territory to be used against India's security interests': Sri Lankan Prez assures Rajnath Singh
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Sri Lanka on Wednesday assured India that the island nation would not allow its territory for "use in activities inimical to India's security interests" even as New Delhi promised upgrading the L70 air defence guns it supplied to the Sri Lankan Air Force.The message was conveyed by Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to Defence Minister Rajnath Singh when Singh called on Dissanayake in Colombo. The two leaders held substantive discussions on issues covering the entire spectrum of the multi-faceted partnership between the two nations.President Dissanayake recalled his interactions with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and reiterated that Sri Lanka would never allow its territory to be used for any activities inimical to India’s security interests, a Defence Ministry spokesperson said, noting that bilateral relations are characterised by traditionally warm relations and mutual trust.His comments assume significance in the backdrop of China making an all out effort to secure and enhance its long-term presence in the island - a move that India opposes sternly. Beijing views Colombo as a key partner in its Belt and Road Initiative while New Delhi views the island as its strategic backyard.Sri Lanka, navigates this rivalry by practising "dual diplomacy" under which it balances ties to leverage economic and infrastructure support from both Asian giants.Sri Lanka Navy rescues 8 people stranded after crossing from India“Secure sea lanes, freedom of navigation, respect for international law and unhindered maritime trade are pivotal for collective security and prosperity of the Indian Ocean Region," Singh said in a veiled reference to China while addressing a meeting attended by Sri Lankan Deputy Minister of Defence Aruna Jayasekara, Commanders of the Sri Lankan Army, Navy and Air Force, and other senior officials.The Defence Minister flagging the need for enhanced cooperation between India and Sri Lanka to shape a secure maritime environment and tackle emerging maritime challenges, before they evolve into serious threats to developmental interests.The two sides also exchanged MoUs on upgradation of L70 air defence guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force. The upgrade will significantly strengthen the air defence architecture of critical assets in Sri Lanka.Later Singh also called on Sri Lankan Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya and visited the Indian Peace Keeping Force memorial in Colombo and paid homage to the soldiers who laid down their lives.The IPKF was a military contingent sent by India to Sri Lanka in July 1987 as part of New Delhi's efforts to disarm the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, a separatist militant organisation, and maintain peace and stability in the region. The memorial pays tribute to the 1,155 IPKF soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty.

primary_source.headline: Delhi building collapse: Three truckloads of debris filled in basement before tragedy, say police
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Three truckloads of debris (malba) were filled into the basement of a five-storey PG building in Delhi's Satya Niketan during renovation work to level it with the ground floor days before its collapse, police said on Wednesday.The labour contractor carrying out the work told police that he was hired by building owner Mahesh Gupta around 10 days before the incident, and was paid Rs 2,800 per day.The contractor, Sanoj Kumar (35), a resident of JJ Camp Moti Bagh and a permanent resident of Manikpur village in Bihar's Banka, was apprehended in Utar Pradesh’s Kasganj and brought to Delhi, where he was arrested and questioned, a senior police officer said."On the day of the incident, a wall on the ground floor that was obstructing space meant for a shop was removed. The building could not withstand the load after the wall was removed and ultimately collapsed," the officer said, even as fresh details emerge as police examine the construction, renovation and maintenance work carried out at the building.Police said the other accused arrested in the case, Sudhanshu Lovneesh (31), a resident of Bhajanpura, was operating the PG in Satya Niketan with his friend Shubham Tyagi on a lease under the name 'Hostel Daze'."Sudhanshu told police that he was a student of Delhi University and running seven PGs in the vicinity. He said he completed his graduation in 2019 and, since 2022, he had been operating PG accommodations in the Satya Niketan area with Tyagi," the officer said.The duo had taken four floors of the building on lease in August 2025 for a monthly rent of Rs 1.05 lakh. They took the property on rent at comparatively lower rates due to its dilapidated condition, he added.Police said Sudhanshu remained indifferent to the construction work being carried out despite knowing that it could affect the building as a whole, the officer said.Three accused -- building owner Mahesh, labour contractor Sanoj Kumar and PG operator Sudhanshu Lovneesh -- were produced before a court and two days' police custody was granted for questioning.Shubham Tyagi is currently absconding, and efforts are underway to trace him, the officer said.The collapse occurred around 1 pm on Sunday, and the police received information at 1.34 pm. The structure, comprising a ground floor and four upper floors, housed several students and other residents.Delhi building collapse: Two-day police custody for owner's son, PG operator, contractorThe incident left seven people, five students and two labourers, dead, and injured five people.Police are also scrutinising the rent agreement under which the PG was being operated.According to a police source, the agreement stated that the PG operators would not be responsible for any "casualties or risk" to tenants.The agreement also purportedly stated that the hostel would not be liable to pay compensation for personal injury, loss or damage to belongings caused by circumstances beyond its control, including sealing, fire, earthquake and heavy rain.The document contained clauses on non-refund of hostel fees and security money and empowered the operators to evict tenants for indiscipline, misconduct, non-payment of dues or other violations.Parents and guardians were also barred from entering tenants' rooms, according to the agreement.Police earlier said the basement had been undergoing repairs for eight to 10 days after waste and water accumulated there following several days of rain. Repair work was also underway on the ground floor for an extension, allegedly for commercial purposes.A Delhi court sent building owner Hariram, an 81-year-old retired Indian Air Force sergeant, and his 75-year-old wife Urmila to 14 days' judicial custody. Their 52-year-old son Mahesh was remanded to police custody for two days.During questioning, Mahesh told police he looked after the building’s maintenance on behalf of his parents.According to the FIR, a local inquiry found that the building was 40-50 years old and that additional floors had been constructed allegedly to generate rental income.  The tragedy has sparked concerns among students living in the South Campus area over the safety of PG accommodations, with many questioning building standards, unauthorised construction and maintenance.Several students left the area after the collapse, with many residents also coming forward and offering water and food for them.  Police said they are continuing to investigate the circumstances leading to the collapse.

primary_source.content: Venice film festival: Barbara Kopple returns with her third film investigating US workers’ rights – this time, undocumented ‘deliveristas’ and the attempts to unionise Amazon staffBarbara Kopple’s documentary about app-based delivery workers is a stirring, defiant, battle-hardened affair, swinging between the fraught picket line and the still more hazardous New York City streets. It’s a new film that feels old in the best sense of the word; a hoarse battle cry that summons the ghosts of The Grapes of Wrath and the New Deal, Eugene Debs and Woody Guthrie. That America is long dead and buried, a casualty of changing times, but Kopple sees no reason why it should not rise again.Union Town, tellingly, is the third part of a loose trilogy which serves as an ongoing audit of US workers’ rights. This began with 1976’s Harlan County, USA, which tackled a Kentucky miners’ strike, and continued through 1990’s American Dream, which covered a meatpacking plant in Austin, Minnesota. Since then, however, the culture has shifted, atomised, with the big corporations increasingly reliant on a shadow economy of undocumented workers. Kopple’s “deliveristas” ferry packages for the likes of Amazon and DoorDash but they are technically third-party contractors. That means if, say, they happen to be injured in the line of duty, they cover the hospital bills and repairs to the bike. It also means that they are likely to be fired while they’re laid up in bed. primary_source.headline: Gains made in TB treatment not enough for 2030 elimination targets in South East Asia: WHO
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The gains made so far in treating tuberculosis in India and other countries in South East Asia are not sufficient enough to hit World Health Organisation’s End TB strategy targets, the UN health body said on Wednesday.The health watchdog also notified that the fund required to eliminate TB is three times less than what is needed at the time.The assessment was made at the ongoing session of the WHO Regional Committee for South-East Asia in Timor-Leste, an independent island nation in Southeast Asia.India, being the biggest and most populous country among 10 other members in the region, was represented by a delegation led by Union Health Minister JP Nadda.While taking note of the progress, WHO said in a statement that with the current gains, the 2030 target of reducing TB incidence by 80 per cent and reduction of TB deaths by 90 per cent seems difficult.Union Health minister JP Nadda holds meeting with MPs from Karnataka, Kerala with focus on eliminating tuberculosisSome positivesSet in 2015, the TB End strategy has resulted in some wins, the health body recounted.“Treatment coverage now exceeds 85%, while treatment success rates are the highest among WHO regions. The rate of development of new TB (incidence) has fallen by 16%, faster than the global average decline of 12%, and TB deaths have fallen by 23%," it said.Still adding new casesDespite the ongoing drive to eliminate the coughing sickness, the WHO South-East Asia Region accounted for 34 per cent of new cases in 2024.The number translates to 3.68 million cases and about 433,000 deaths.This region is reportedly home to almost a quarter of the world’s population.Problem of resistanceTuberculosis is a bacterial illness and the one affected depends on antibiotics to get better.However, with the rampant antimicrobial resistance, around 150,000 people have developed multidrug and rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis.This has made the treatment more trickier than usual and the number represents more than 38 per cent of the global burden.Funds not sufficientAccording to the World Health Organization Regional Office for South-East Asia, TB financing has fallen much short of what is needed at the present.“In 2024, approximately $900 million was available for the regional TB response, against an estimated need of around $3 billion,” it said.With funds remaining below the needed bar, ministers and officials from member states have called for stronger domestic resource mobilisation, more efficient use of available resources, pooled procurement and regional collaboration to improve access to quality-assured medicines, diagnostics and other essential commodities.Financial hit for the familyAccording to the Lancet, tuberculosis is widely called the ‘disease of poverty’ as it thrives in economically challenged circumstances and further deepens the financial struggles of those affected by it.Evidence has shown that many patients are not able to hold jobs and may lose income in the very moment they needed it the most.Treatment coverage rate of 92 per centAccording to the Union Health Ministry, India has recorded a 21% decline in TB incidence between 2015 and 2024, nearly twice the global pace.&nbsp;The country has also achieved a treatment coverage rate of 92%, as per the WHO Global TB Report 2025.Though more TB patients are receiving treatment, the coverage fell short of achieving its self imposed elimination deadline of December 2025 as announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in 2018.

stories.primary_headline: NIH to use part of its budget to pay for Department of Defense research

primary_source.headline: NIH to use part of its budget to pay for Department of Defense research
primary_source.content:
Late last week, word started leaking that the National Institutes of Health (NIH) had reached an agreement with the Department of Defense that would see part of the NIH's budget used to fund research at the Department of Defense. So, on the Friday just prior to a US holiday weekend, the Department of Defense released a copy of the agreement and confirmed that it had been signed roughly a month earlier. The move is striking for a number of reasons, ranging from the existing budget disparities between the two parties involved to the fact that the money would be used for projects that the current NIH leadership has explicitly rejected.
The agreement itself sets up a system where the NIH would transfer money to the Department of Defense to fund staff and projects that would "support the advanced development of medical countermeasures against pandemic influenza, chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) threats, and emerging infectious diseases." The money would come out of the budget for the NIH's National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, or NIAID, to which Congress has allocated $6.6 billion in 2026. The agreement is set to run for a decade.
Left unspecified is just how much of the NIAID budget will be spent on Defense projects. Reporting by Nature suggests that the Department of Defense was looking for up to a third of its total budget but was being told to settle for about 10 percent. There's obviously an enormous disparity between the budgets of these two agencies, given that the 2026 Defense budget is roughly $1 trillion. That budget is under considerable strain, however, due to the open-ended nature of the conflict with Iran. The deal has also been announced at a time when the NIH has been struggling to issue sufficient grants to use the money that Congress allocated to it.Read full article

sources.headline: Saudi Arabia Runs Out of Easy Routes for Oil to Bypass Iran War

stories.brief: Saudi Arabia is facing an acute logistical crisis as escalating regional tensions threaten the security of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical maritime chokepoint for global energy supplies. With oil prices surging past the $100-per-barrel threshold, the Kingdom’s reliance on traditional maritime export routes has become a significant vulnerability, forcing Riyadh to scramble for alternative, yet increasingly limited, pipeline infrastructure. The potential for a direct conflict involving Iran has effectively neutralized the safety of these primary shipping lanes, causing a precipitous decline in export volumes as market uncertainty intensifies. This geopolitical bottleneck is not merely a supply chain disruption but a fundamental challenge to Saudi Arabia’s ability to maintain its market share while navigating the volatile security landscape of the Persian Gulf. Consequently, the Kingdom is forced to weigh the economic costs of reduced output against the existential risks posed by regional instability, highlighting the precarious nature of global energy security in an era of heightened geopolitical friction. This situation signals a potential paradigm shift in global energy markets, where the weaponization of maritime chokepoints could trigger sustained inflationary pressure and force a rapid, albeit chaotic, diversification of global energy supply chains. It underscores the fragility of current oil logistics and the urgent need for consuming nations to reassess their dependency on vulnerable transit corridors.

primary_source.headline: Ethanol blending: Govt plans flexi-fuel vehicles beyond E20, says PM's advisor
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The government is preparing to allow ethanol blending beyond the current E20 level through the rollout of flexi-fuel vehicles, Prime Minister’s Advisor Tarun Kapoor said on Wednesday.Addressing an event here, Kapoor described the E20 programme as “very successful.”&nbsp;Several automobile makers have announced plans to introduce flexi-fuel vehicles soon.Supreme Court turns down petition for mandatory disclosure of ethanol content in petrol at fuel pumps“Now our focus is on going into flexi-fuel vehicles and allowing blending at a percentage which will be higher than E20,” he said, stressing the need to expand pure ethanol availability at fuel outlets alongside the vehicle rollout.The biofuels push has gained urgency amid the West Asia crisis, which has disrupted supplies and driven crude oil prices to nearly USD 100 a barrel. “It is important that we try to have whatever is available in the country,” Kapoor noted.Ethanol production capacity has already surpassed blending requirements, requiring the industry to find additional uses for the surplus. Responding to recent criticism of E20, he attributed much of it to misinformation or motivated reasons. Studies show the blend performs well, with any marginal drop in fuel efficiency offset by higher octane.On the diesel side, the government is exploring biofuel-based additives, including experiments with isobutanol that could create a major new avenue.&nbsp;Kapoor also highlighted the GOBARdhan scheme, which consolidates incentives to boost compressed biogas (CBG), and urged ethanol producers to diversify into CBG and value-added products such as potash.

stories.brief: Prime Minister’s Advisor Tarun Kapoor has announced that the Indian government is preparing to expand ethanol blending beyond the current E20 threshold by facilitating the rollout of flexi-fuel vehicles. This strategic pivot aims to capitalize on the country’s surplus ethanol production capacity, which has already outpaced existing blending mandates, while simultaneously reducing reliance on volatile global crude oil markets currently strained by the West Asia crisis. Kapoor emphasized that the government is actively collaborating with automobile manufacturers to introduce compatible vehicles and is working to ensure the widespread availability of pure ethanol at fuel outlets. Addressing concerns regarding fuel efficiency, he dismissed criticisms of the E20 program as largely unfounded, noting that performance trade-offs are negligible. Furthermore, the government is diversifying its biofuel strategy by exploring isobutanol additives for diesel and promoting the GOBARdhan scheme to incentivize compressed biogas production, signaling a comprehensive shift toward domestic energy security and sustainable industrial diversification. This policy shift signals a decisive move toward energy independence by insulating the domestic economy from global oil price volatility while creating a robust, diversified biofuel ecosystem that supports both the automotive sector and agricultural value chains.

primary_source.headline: US Treasury to Buy Up to $6 Billion in Long-Dated Debt
primary_source.content: The US Treasury will purchase up to $6 billion of longer-dated government debt in the first operation under an expanded buybacks program. It's part of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's effort to stem the rise in borrowing costs. Bloomberg's Michael McKee has the breaking news and immediate market reaction. (Source: Bloomberg)

sources.headline: US Treasury to Buy Up to $6 Billion in Long-Dated Debt

stories.brief: The United States Treasury has officially initiated its expanded buyback program, announcing plans to purchase up to $6 billion in longer-dated government debt. This strategic intervention, spearheaded by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, marks a significant shift in fiscal management aimed at curbing the recent, concerning escalation in borrowing costs that has pressured financial markets. By actively repurchasing these securities, the Treasury seeks to enhance market liquidity and smooth out volatility in the yield curve, signaling a proactive stance on managing the federal debt profile. This operation represents the first major execution of the expanded buyback initiative, which was designed to provide the government with greater flexibility in debt management. As the Treasury Department navigates a complex macroeconomic environment characterized by fluctuating interest rates and fiscal pressures, this move underscores a deliberate effort to stabilize the secondary market for government bonds and maintain investor confidence in the face of rising debt service obligations. This intervention signals a pivotal shift toward more active fiscal management, aiming to suppress yield volatility and reduce the government's long-term interest expense burden. By stabilizing the Treasury market, the administration hopes to prevent broader financial contagion and ensure that rising debt levels do not destabilize the wider economy.

primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: While the Congress government in Kerala is awaiting legal opinion on the further steps to be taken on the Enforcement Directorate (ED) letter seeking registration of a Rs. 3.28 crore bribery case against former CM Pinarayi Vijayan, Vijayan termed the ED findings as a 'shameful narrative'.Vijayan, who got angry when journalists sought his opinion on the ED move, later said at a public function that ED's attempts to target him won't work as there were no illegal deals involved."My life in an open book. The outcome will likely reshape the state's political alliances and test the credibility of central investigative agencies in the eyes of the Kerala electorate.

primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: While any uncertainties in the Gulf countries earlier used to have its direct impact on Kerala's real estate sector as non-resident Indians (NRIs) used to be the major investors, the crisis in the Gulf sector these days is not affecting Kerala's real estate sector.Thanks to the increased purchase capacity of the local people and the easy availability of bank loans.Soaring heat, inadequate rains plunge Kerala into acute crisis: State imposes up to one hour power cutsAccording to real estate industry sources, a major chunk of customers of flats in Kerala these days are local private and government sector employees."Earlier around 80 per cent of flat buyers used to be NRIs and 20 per cent local customers. Now it is 80 per cent local customers and 20 per cent NRIs," said Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations (CREDAI) of India executive council member S N Raghuchandran Nair.The increasing income level of the government employees and those in the private sector is considered to be a key factor.&nbsp;The average annual salaries in Kerala government service is now close to Rs 10 lakhs. Of the 5.54 lakh government employees, over two lakh are drawing more than Rs 12 lakhs per annum. Hence the disposable income of individuals, as well as couples with both of them working, keeps increasing.Banks are also aggressively campaigning customers to avail home loans and the Income Tax exemptions for home loans too prompt local people to invest in the sector.According to the State Level Bankers Committee data, banks in Kerala sanctioned Rs. 56,490.92 crores to 6,61,426 beneficiaries till March 2026 as against Rs 43,359.44 crore to 6,09,010 beneficiaries till March 2025.Increasing trend of NRIs permanently migrating to foreign countries, investing in gold or business ventures as well as in real estate in countries where they work are also reasons for the changing trend in the investments in the real estate sector in Kerala."There could also be a stagnation in the NRI investments in the real estate sector. Hence many seem to be investing in gold or similar easier options. Migration to other countries is also a reason for the decline in NRI investments in Kerala's real estate sector," said migration analyst S Irudaya Rajan, who is chair of the International Institute of Migration and Development in Thiruvananthapuram.While many NRIs used to leave flats unoccupied, many local buyers are generating decent income from flats by renting out, said Nair.Nair also said that introduction of Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA) has also enhanced the credibility of the sector.&nbsp;A total of 60,526 residential units have been registered with the K-RERA since it started registration in 2021.

sources.headline: Kerala real estate: Local buyers overtake NRIs as home sales gain momentum

stories.brief: Kerala’s real estate sector is undergoing a structural transformation, shifting from a historical reliance on Non-Resident Indian (NRI) investment to a market dominated by local buyers. According to the Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (CREDAI), the buyer demographic has inverted, with local private and government employees now accounting for 80 percent of flat purchases, a stark reversal from previous trends. This shift is primarily driven by rising disposable incomes among state government and private sector employees, coupled with aggressive bank lending and tax incentives that have democratized home ownership. Conversely, NRI investment has stagnated as expatriates increasingly prioritize permanent migration, gold, or foreign business ventures over domestic property. Furthermore, the implementation of the Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (K-RERA) has bolstered market credibility, encouraging local buyers to view real estate as a viable, income-generating asset rather than an unoccupied investment, thereby insulating the state’s property market from volatility in Gulf economies. This decoupling of Kerala’s real estate market from Gulf economic volatility signals a more resilient, domestically-driven economy that reduces the state's vulnerability to external geopolitical shocks. It reflects a maturing middle class capable of sustaining long-term infrastructure and housing demand independently of remittance-based capital flows.

stories.brief: Authorities in Jangareddygudem have apprehended three senior officials from the Bank of Baroda—the branch manager, joint manager, and credit officer—following an investigation into a sophisticated gold-loan fraud scheme. The arrests were triggered by the earlier detention of a gold appraiser, whose involvement exposed a systematic operation where genuine gold ornaments pledged as collateral were surreptitiously replaced with counterfeit items within the bank's secure lockers. Police investigations have successfully recovered 4.12 kilograms of gold and ₹10 lakh in cash, confirming the scale of the illicit activity conducted under the guise of legitimate banking operations. This breach of trust highlights significant lapses in internal audit protocols and security oversight, as the very personnel entrusted with safeguarding assets were actively facilitating the embezzlement. The incident has prompted a broader review of the bank's operational integrity and risk management frameworks to prevent further exploitation of the gold-loan portfolio. This incident exposes critical vulnerabilities in financial institution internal controls, potentially triggering stricter regulatory audits and a loss of public confidence in gold-backed lending products. It underscores the urgent need for enhanced digital verification and independent oversight mechanisms to mitigate insider threats within the banking sector.

This market reaction highlights the fragility of investor confidence in Treasury debt management and suggests that future interventions may require greater transparency or scale to effectively mitigate volatility. Failure to align policy actions with market expectations risks exacerbating yield instability, potentially complicating the government's broader fiscal and borrowing objectives.

primary_source.content: National security 'can't come at the expense of social security', says Burnham Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch pressed Burnham over whether he would spend 3% of GDP on defence by 2030 and how he would pay for this. This debate underscores a fundamental tension in British politics between maintaining robust military capabilities in an unstable geopolitical climate and managing domestic fiscal pressures. primary_source.headline: NOAA is putting commercial fishing ahead of conservation
primary_source.content:
In July, the Trump administration relegated endangered leatherback turtles, sea lions, and whales to mere collateral damage in its race to profit from the oceans. Now, fisheries science is in the government’s crosshairs.
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) announced new agency priorities last week that they say are a commitment to “cutting bureaucracy, modernizing our science, and putting our fishing communities first.” But experts say the agency’s actions will erode fish stocks, threaten endangered species, and surrender marine habitats to destructive trawlers.
The agency-level reforms serve as a self-proclaimed “operational roadmap” to fulfilling President Donald Trump’s “Restoring American Seafood Competitiveness” executive order, signed in April 2025.Read full article

While NOAA leadership frames these reforms as a necessary modernization effort to reduce bureaucratic hurdles and bolster fishing communities, environmental experts and conservationists warn that the policy shift prioritizes industrial profit over critical ecological safeguards. By streamlining regulatory processes, the agency risks facilitating the expansion of destructive trawling practices that threaten vulnerable marine populations, including endangered leatherback turtles, sea lions, and various whale species. This strategic pivot signals a fundamental realignment of NOAA’s mission, moving away from its traditional role as a steward of marine biodiversity and toward a model that treats ocean ecosystems primarily as economic resources. Consequently, the agency faces intense scrutiny over the long-term sustainability of fish stocks and the potential for irreversible damage to protected marine habitats. This policy shift marks a significant departure from science-based conservation, potentially triggering long-term collapse in fish stocks and biodiversity loss that could undermine the very industry it seeks to support. It establishes a precedent where executive economic mandates override environmental protections, likely leading to protracted legal battles and a permanent degradation of federal marine oversight.

primary_source.content: Patna: Ever since the Vigilance Intelligence Bureau (VIB) sleuths in Bihar have launched a crackdown against corrupt officials, including police officers, the Babus in the State have adopted a new methodology to accept bribes.These officers neither ask for illegal gratification on phone nor directly ask the cash amount as bribe money. Instead, they use new secret codes like ‘ek bora chawal’, ‘ek peti’, ‘tel-paani’ to accept bribes and escape the VIB dragnet.Bihar sees grim flood scenes as 22 lakh people affected across 12 districts; CM conducts aerial surveySample this:Case I: A person who was charged with assault in a local police station in Patna had to hand over a “sack full of rice” to get his name deleted. ‘A sack full of rice’, which, in Hindi, is termed as ‘ek bora chawal’ is the new code word for Rs 1 lakh demanded by the Investigating Officer (IO) Ajit Kumar Singh. The mother of the accused spoke to the IO, struck the deal and handed over the audio call recording to the Vigilance Investigation Bureau sleuths, who, after verification, trapped and arrested the cop.Case II: Recently, a Revenue and Land Reforms official Kanchan Kumari Jha was arrested by the Vigilance sleuths after her servant, serving as an agent accepting bribe on behalf of ‘Madam’, asked for a washing machine and Rs 2 lakh to clear a land related case.Case III: One Municipal Corporation employee, who retired recently, was asked to cough up ‘ek peti’ to get his Provident Fund (PF) and gratuity cleared. The code: ‘Ek peti’ means Rs 1 lakh. The retired person struck the deal through the code and handed over the audio recording to the VIB, which eventually trapped and arrested the official.Case IV: A girl was kidnapped in Bihar’s Vaishali district. Her family members, seeking recovery of the girl, ran helter skelter but the police investigation did not move further till the Investigation Officer (IO) used the code: ‘Tel paani’ to seek bribe from the hapless family. ‘Tel paani’ is the code for Rs 10,000 which the family handed over to the IO but at the same time informed the VIB. The IO, Meghnath Ram, was eventually trapped and arrested.“Under the new law, audio recording is valid evidence if the sample voice matches during the voice test and may help in conviction,” said a senior investigating official.

Despite these obfuscation tactics, the VIB has successfully apprehended multiple offenders, including police officers and land reform officials, by leveraging audio recordings provided by whistleblowers and victims. Under current legal frameworks, these recordings serve as admissible evidence once voice samples are verified, proving instrumental in securing arrests. This cat-and-mouse dynamic highlights the persistent nature of systemic corruption within the state bureaucracy and the evolving investigative methodologies required to dismantle these entrenched illicit networks. The shift toward coded bribery signals a sophisticated adaptation by corrupt actors to evade modern surveillance, necessitating more advanced intelligence-gathering techniques from anti-corruption agencies. If left unchecked, this normalization of coded illicit transactions threatens to erode public trust in state institutions and complicates the judicial process for prosecuting systemic graft.

primary_source.content: New Delhi: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued comprehensive guidelines making median and avenue plantation mandatory and integral to National Highway development and project completion.The norms require plantation strictly as per contract agreements, the Green Highways Policy 2015 and other Ministry of Road Transport and Highways directives.A key provision sets a minimum threshold for Provisional Certificate of Completion (PCC) or Provisional Commercial Operation Date (PCOD). Projects will qualify only if plantation covers at least 80% of the available Right of Way earmarked for greening, with saplings showing a minimum 90% survival rate at inspection, the statement said. 'Why not install cameras, monitoring rooms at toll plazas': Supreme Court to NHAIAny shortfall beyond 80% must be flagged with clear timelines. Financial withholdings under the relevant agreements will continue until the full target is met.During the operations and maintenance period, release of O&M or annuity payments in EPC, HAM and BOT Annuity projects, as well as maintenance compliance assessments in BOT-Toll projects, will depend on sustaining a 90% survival rate. Dead plants must be replaced promptly with specimens of similar age and growth to maintain uniform density.NHAI seeks new toll agency for Electronics City e-way, eyes Rs 265 crore per yearNHAI will seek verification from its environment and plantation experts before processing payments or certifying compliance, the statement added. primary_source.content: Bengaluru: When Shreyas Iyer replaced the World Cup-winning Suryakumar Yadav as the T20I captain of the Indian team this June, it was viewed as the proper change of guard. After leading Kolkata Knight Riders to their third Indian Premier League (IPL) triumph in 2024, Iyer did wonders at a hitherto underperforming Punjab Kings the previous two seasons, leading them to back to back play-offs, including the final in 2025. Suryakumar Yadav’s slump opens door for Shreyas Iyer in T20 squadWith runs going completely dry from Suryakumar’s bat and banished from the Indian team, the road was perfectly laid for Iyer to take complete the change.It has, however, been a brutal initiation for Iyer in international captaincy. India were stunningly whitewashed 2-0 by Ireland in his first series, and worse was to follow in the ensuing series against England, where the Men In Blue lost 0-4, with one of the games washed out. Iyer finally got on board against Zimbabwe, India winning it 3-0. Since then Iyer has had time to reflect on the shortcomings and work on them as he gears up to lead India at the Asian Games starting September 19, where they are the defending champions.It’s safe to assume Iyer will be under pressure to deliver at the continental bash, where India have got a direct quarterfinal berth and need to win three games on the bounce to retain their gold. The legendary Sunil Gavaskar was confident of Iyer coming up to the goods in Japan.“I think he's very experienced as a captain. We've seen him when he was captain of KKR, Delhi Capitals, and then Punjab. He's got the experience. I don't think there’s going to be any further pressure on him. That said, I think every time you captain India, the expectations are very high,” said Gavaskar in an interaction with the select media arranged by Sony Sports Network.‘Shot selection is very important’: Sunil Gavaskar“I think everybody who&nbsp;gets the honour and privilege of captaining the country recognises that, you know, the pressure of expectations will always be there. I don’t really think he’s going to have any pressure going into the Asian Games. So, it's not going to be easy at all.”With Japan not being a cricket-playing country, there are reservations about the quality of pitches it will dole out. Reports have also emerged about the lack of quality dressing rooms. Gavaskar felt cricketers shouldn’t have a hard time coping with it because many have grown up encountering such conditions.“I think the beauty of cricket is that when you play club cricket in your cities, your dressing rooms are just tents in which you change and go out to bat. The outfields are not necessarily the best. But this is when you're starting to come up the ladder. So, in a way, you're used to playing in conditions that are not exactly like international venues where cricket is played regularly. And I think that is the challenge. To conquer that challenge and to win will be even more special.”Indian audience can catch the Asian Games 2026 live action on on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV.

stories.brief: Delhi University, one of India’s premier academic institutions, faces a chronic infrastructure deficit as the limited capacity of its on-campus hostels fails to accommodate the surging influx of outstation students. This systemic shortage forces thousands of undergraduates to navigate the unregulated and often exorbitant private Paying Guest (PG) and rental markets surrounding the campus, effectively shifting the burden of student housing onto the private sector. While the university administration struggles to expand residential facilities, students are left vulnerable to fluctuating rental prices, inconsistent living standards, and the logistical challenges of securing safe, affordable accommodation in a competitive urban environment. This reliance on private housing not only exacerbates the financial strain on families but also highlights a critical disconnect between the university's enrollment expansion policies and its capacity to provide essential student support services. Consequently, the lack of institutional oversight in the private housing market creates a precarious living situation that fundamentally alters the student experience and accessibility to education. The inability of public institutions to provide adequate housing creates a socioeconomic barrier to entry, effectively prioritizing affluent students who can afford private market premiums while marginalizing those from lower-income backgrounds. This infrastructure gap threatens the university's mandate for inclusive education and necessitates urgent policy intervention to regulate private housing or accelerate campus development.

stories.brief: The European Commission has unveiled a strategic proposal aimed at overhauling public procurement regulations to incentivize European authorities and public bodies to prioritize domestic goods and services. This initiative, designed to bolster the bloc’s economic sovereignty, seeks to counter the growing influence of Chinese competitors in the European market by encouraging a "Buy European" approach. While the proposals stop short of implementing mandatory binding quotas, they represent a significant shift in EU policy, signaling a more assertive stance on industrial protectionism and economic security. By leveraging the massive scale of public spending, Brussels aims to strengthen local supply chains and reduce dependency on non-EU entities, particularly those backed by state-subsidized models. This move reflects a broader geopolitical trend where the European Union is increasingly prioritizing internal economic resilience and competitive parity in response to global market distortions and the aggressive expansion of foreign state-backed enterprises. This policy shift marks a pivotal transition toward economic protectionism, potentially reshaping global trade dynamics by forcing foreign firms to navigate a more restrictive European procurement landscape. It underscores the EU's commitment to safeguarding its industrial base against state-subsidized competition, likely triggering reciprocal trade tensions and accelerating the fragmentation of global supply chains.

stories.brief: The average interest rate for a 30-year fixed mortgage in the United States has surged to its highest level since June 2025, signaling a tightening of credit conditions that continues to challenge the housing market's recovery. This upward trajectory in borrowing costs, driven by persistent inflationary pressures and shifting expectations regarding Federal Reserve monetary policy, has effectively sidelined many prospective homebuyers who are already grappling with limited inventory and elevated property valuations. Financial institutions and mortgage lenders are responding to the broader macroeconomic environment by adjusting risk premiums, further exacerbating the affordability crisis for first-time buyers. As mortgage applications decline in response to these prohibitive rates, the real estate sector faces a period of stagnation, forcing industry analysts to recalibrate their forecasts for housing starts and overall economic growth. This development underscores the delicate balance the central bank must maintain as it attempts to curb inflation without precipitating a deeper contraction in the residential property market. This sustained rise in mortgage rates threatens to lock in a long-term housing supply shortage while cooling consumer spending, potentially slowing broader economic momentum as household budgets are increasingly diverted toward debt servicing. It signals a prolonged period of market recalibration where affordability remains the primary barrier to entry for a significant segment of the population.

This surge has forced traditional parties, including the governing coalition and the opposition CDU, to grapple with the erosion of their voter bases and the necessity of recalibrating their platforms to address populist grievances. As the AfD secures significant vote shares in state elections, the political environment has become increasingly polarized, complicating coalition building and threatening the stability of the traditional consensus-based governance model that has defined post-war German politics for decades. This shift signals a profound realignment in European politics, reflecting broader continental trends of rising nationalism and skepticism toward established institutional authority. The AfD’s rise threatens to paralyze German legislative processes through increased polarization and complicates the European Union’s unified policy stance on critical issues like migration and climate change. It forces a structural realignment of German politics that could destabilize the traditional centrist coalition model, potentially leading to long-term governance gridlock.

This narrative challenges the conventional perception of layoffs as purely catastrophic events, illustrating how corporate compensation structures can create unintended financial buffers for employees. It also underscores the necessity for tech firms to carefully calibrate severance and equity policies to balance fiscal responsibility with employee relations during periods of significant organizational restructuring.

It underscores a broader transition toward transactional geopolitics where emerging economies must increasingly prioritize domestic resilience over traditional trade alliances.

primary_source.content: For decades, I had been haunted by paruresis, an inability to urinate in public toilets. But that day of nakedness suddenly, surprisingly, led me to shed my inhibitionsFor as long as I can remember, I’ve suffered from a condition called paruresis – also known as shy bladder syndrome. This means that, unless I’m alone in public toilets, I cannot pee, however badly I need to go. I developed tactics to deal with this, such as loitering outside the gents if I see someone going in, so that I can walk in as they walk out. But if someone follows me in, I find I’m just standing there, which I worry looks odd.I’m a writer, so am often out and about meeting people in cafes, hotels and at events. My agricultural background means I also meet a lot of my interviewees on farms – but at least there I could pop behind a hedge if I needed to go, and be assured of privacy. Continue reading...

primary_source.content: Far-right parties, Maga ideology and Kremlin money are conniving to suffocate liberal idealism for another generationNot all that long ago, Europe was a beacon of liberal idealism. One memoir recalls it as an era “comfortably saturated with confidence in the unfailing and binding power of tolerance and conciliation”. The economic system seemed obviously preferable to barbarous alternatives. “People honestly believed that the divergencies and the boundaries between nations and sects would gradually melt away into a common humanity,” the author added.Those words could describe the spirit of globalisation at the turn of the millennium. Ultimately, Behr suggests that unless European nations actively confront these coalescing threats, they risk repeating the catastrophic historical cycle that Zweig documented before his death, potentially suffocating liberal values for an entire generation. The erosion of liberal consensus across Europe signals a profound geopolitical shift that threatens to dismantle the post-WWII international order, potentially realigning the continent toward authoritarianism and isolationism. This trend undermines the stability of Western alliances and invites a return to the volatile, nationalist-driven conflicts that defined the early 20th century.

primary_source.content: Ailsworth, Cambridgeshire: Trifid bur-marigold is struggling nationally, but thanks to a little ‘Goldilocks’ land management, it has the perfect conditions hereAfter a night of storms, the air feels freshly washed. I breathe in delicious scents of damp grass, earth, and sweet, winey blackberry from hedges weighed down with a bumper harvest. Once again, I’m drawn to the River Nene, a ribbon of blue and green that snakes lazily through the valley. I stand for a while on the bridge over Ailsworth weir, where water spills and chatters over bright green swathes of river water-crowfoot. For a moment its steady white noise overpowers the nearby A1.The main river is slow and silent, yet its margins are bright with flowers: purple loosestrife, marsh woundwort, water mint, water forget-me-not and celery-leaved buttercup. Together they make a loose embroidery of mauve, blue and yellow among the green – quite the contrast from the scorched gold fields I’ve become used to. But the plant that catches my eye is trifid bur-marigold, with its understated, button-like golden flowers. Its name comes from its mostly three-part leaves and fruits that are tipped with barbed bristles, ready to hitch a lift on passing cattle, dogs, maybe an otter, or even humans. Continue reading...

Lambert’s observations highlight the critical role of environmental stewardship in preserving biodiversity, as the trifid bur-marigold utilizes its unique, barbed seeds to propagate through passing wildlife. By maintaining these specific riverine conditions, local conservation efforts are successfully shielding vulnerable plant species from broader national decline, demonstrating how micro-level interventions can effectively counteract the negative impacts of regional environmental stress. This narrative underscores the efficacy of localized, precision land management in mitigating the effects of climate volatility on biodiversity. It serves as a replicable model for conservationists aiming to protect endangered flora by creating resilient, micro-climate refugia within larger, stressed ecosystems.

primary_source.content: But Erin Atkinson has already decided what should happen to her money and belongings when she dies. primary_source.content: The startup’s soaring valuation signals that VCs still see room for multiple major players to capture meaningful market share in AI coding, one of the technology’s most significant applications. Cognition said that since announcing its last fundraise in May, its annualized run-rate revenue has grown from $492 million to $900 million. While the startup didn’t explain how it calculates that run-rate revenue, the metric is usually defined as a month’s top line multiplied by 12. Cursor, another popular coding assistant, was in talks in April to raise capital at a $50 billion valuation before agreeing to sell to SpaceX for $60 billion later that month. At the time of the funding talks, Cursor’s annualized revenue had surpassed $2 billion. This means Cognition currently commands a higher revenue multiple than Cursor did in the spring. Like Cursor did before joining SpaceX, Cognition is training its own model based on open source alternatives. Over time, reducing its reliance on expensive third-party models from OpenAI and Anthropic will help cut costs and bring the company closer to breakeven. Cognition is expected to reach $4 billion to $5 billion in annualized revenue by the end of 2026, according to The Information. By comparison, TechCrunch reported in the spring that Cursor was on track to surpass $6 billion by year-end. Still, it’s notable that a16z, a major backer of Cursor, which made a killing when it sold to SpaceX, is back to lead a round in a Cursor competitor. Founded in 2024 by math prodigy Scott Wu, Cognition counts Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Citi among its major enterprise customers. primary_source.headline: Supreme Court forces TV stations to sell more election ads at steep discounts
primary_source.content:
In a victory for Republican campaign committees, the Supreme Court issued an order on Friday that forces broadcast TV stations to cut the prices of election ads purchased by political parties and joint fundraising committees. The September 4 ruling came in response to a petition filed by the National Republican Congressional Committee and National Republican Senatorial Committee.
The Supreme Court order was issued just in time for the start of a 60-day period before the election, in which broadcasters are required by US law to offer ad discounts to individual candidates. Because of the top court's order, TV stations must also give their lowest ad rates to political parties and joint fundraising committees, which face fewer limits on how much money they can raise and spend.
The legally required discount is known as the “lowest unit charge,” or LUC. A US law that applies to any licensed station that airs election ads requires that the lowest price be charged for “the use of any broadcasting station by any person who is a legally qualified candidate for any public office in connection with his campaign.” The main legal question is whether “use… by” a candidate can refer to ad time purchased on a candidate’s behalf by parties and joint fundraising committees.Read full article

primary_source.content:
Meta took days to remove ads containing AI-generated child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on Facebook and Instagram. Some ads featured photos of real kids, including a press photo of a young member of a European royal family and images swiped from a popular Instagram profile of a preteen girl deemed an influencer.
In an investigation published Tuesday, the Tech Transparency Project (TTP) reported that Meta failed to detect 332 ads containing CSAM this year. The “vast majority” of ads promoted AI apps made in China, while many ads promoted so-called “nudify” apps that make it easy for bad actors to use AI and digitally alter images of children.
TTP matched “multiple CSAM ads to photos of real children that appeared online.” These ads seem to violate federal child pornography laws, since the Justice Department has clarified that AI CSAM is just as harmful as CSAM. The young royal’s image was “animated into a video of her performing a graphic sex act,” TTP found. Other ads animated a photo of a 14-year-old Instagram influencer “showing off her new sports club uniform” into “a video of her performing oral sex.” A third “preteen” victim “posing in a pink athletic outfit with pigtails” in a series of stock photos was morphed into a video where she looks frightened as she’s molested by an adult male, TTP reported.Read full article

primary_source.content:
As the world's largest search engine, Google is often a target of Europe's Digital Markets Act (DMA), which seeks to rein in Big Tech. The European Commission hit Google with a hefty 460 million euro ($543 million) fine in July for preferring its own services in searches for travel and shopping. Google has now made changes in accordance with the European Union's wishes, but it claims the result is a massive reduction in search quality.
If you don't live in Europe and perform a search for, say, hotels, Google will helpfully provide myriad sponsored links, booking recommendations, and price-comparison tools in its results. The problem is that this content isn't organic—Google includes links and offers contingent on its business interests. To get to the regular search results for these types of lucrative searches, you have to scroll way down the page. Companies that partner with Google can get more exposure, but the European Commission says this creates an unlevel playing field.
"To comply with DMA requirements, we're making significant changes to Search in Europe," Google's Nick Fox told Reuters. "These changes ​degrade the user experience for ​Europeans, boosting online intermediaries ⁠at the expense of local businesses and removing helpful features people rely on every day."Read full article

stories.brief: The United States Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) has experienced a significant drawdown of 1.2 million barrels, pushing national emergency oil stockpiles to their lowest levels since 1982. This reduction, reported by the Department of Energy, reflects ongoing federal efforts to manage domestic energy prices and mitigate supply chain volatility amidst fluctuating global market conditions. While the administration maintains that these releases are necessary to stabilize the energy sector and provide relief to consumers facing inflationary pressures, the sustained depletion of the reserve has sparked intense debate regarding national energy security. Critics argue that the continued reliance on the SPR to address short-term market imbalances leaves the nation increasingly vulnerable to potential geopolitical shocks or sudden supply disruptions. As the reserve reaches these historic lows, policymakers face mounting pressure to balance immediate economic stabilization strategies with the long-term imperative of maintaining a robust emergency buffer capable of insulating the country against future energy crises. The depletion of the SPR to four-decade lows significantly narrows the government's capacity to respond to future supply shocks, potentially increasing market volatility and geopolitical risk. This trend forces a critical reassessment of the balance between using emergency reserves for short-term price management versus preserving them for genuine national security contingencies.
